title: "Changing the Dataframe"
format: live-html
engine: knitr
---



::: {.cell autorun='false'}

```{.webr .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
df <- read_csv("titanic.csv")
```
:::




# mutate()
We want to work with `Fare`, but we want to round everything up to integers. We can add a new column to the dataframe. Column names can't be repeated, so we'll name our new column `Rounded_Fare` 

ceiling() is a function that rounds its inputs to the nearest whole number. 




::: {.cell autorun='false'}

```{.webr .cell-code}
df %>% mutate(Rounded_Fare = ceiling(Fare))
```
:::




We can apply whatever transformation we want within the parantheses of mutate()




::: {.cell autorun='false'}

```{.webr .cell-code}
df %>% mutate(Fare_Plus_One = Fare + 1)
```
:::




### Directly adding column to dataframe 
To save the new column to the dataframe, you must reassign the variable. 



::: {.cell autorun='false'}

```{.webr .cell-code}
df <- df %>% mutate(Rounded_Fare = ceiling(Fare))
```
:::




Try seeing the changes we made to `df` with the head() function. 

### Making a new dataframe with our changes
Sometimes we want to keep the original dataframe, so we make a new dataframe with our edits. Remember that we have to name our new dataframe something new. 



::: {.cell autorun='false'}

```{.webr .cell-code}
df_with_rounded <- df %>% mutate(Rounded_Fare = ceiling(Fare))
```
:::




## if_else()
We can also use conditional statements to generate new columns. Let's say we want a column that indicates whether a passenger was an adult (`Age >= 18`)

We can use the if_else() function, which requires three inputs, in this order: (1) the condition (2) the value if the condition is met (3) the value if the condition is not met. 




::: {.cell autorun='false'}

```{.webr .cell-code}
df_adult <- df %>% mutate(Is_Adult = if_else(Age >= 18, "Yes", "No"))
```
:::




### Dealing with unknown values 
You may notice that some values in `Is_Adult` column are neither "Yes" or "No", but something called NA instead. We get this value when the value in `Age` was missing, so R can't determine whether or not the value is greater or equal to 18. 

We can deal with this by adding another input into the if_else() function: `missing = "Unknown"`




::: {.cell autorun='false'}

```{.webr .cell-code}
df_adult <- df %>% mutate(Is_Adult = if_else(Age >= 18, "Yes", "No", missing = "Unknown"))
```
:::




Now, instead of NA as the value, the missing values will have an actual value. 

## case_when()
if_else() is helpful when we only have two conditions, but we may have more than two. 




::: {.cell autorun='false'}

```{.webr .cell-code}
df %>% mutate(Age_Group = case_when(
  Age < 13 ~ "Child",
  Age < 18 ~ "Teen",
  Age >= 18 ~ "Adult",
  .default = "Unknown"
))
```
:::
